title: Knowledge & RAG
markdown:
Retrieval is handled by `openexecutive.knowledge.retriever.retrieve`, querying ChromaDB collections through `openexecutive.knowledge.store.ChromaDBStore`. Five collections back the system:

- **BUILTIN** — curated MBA-style domain knowledge shipped with the repo.
- **COMPANY** — customer documents ingested via the `/documents` endpoint. Curated uploads only — synced Notion pages do not land here.
- **NOTION_WIKI** — optional Notion sync (`NOTION_SYNC_ENABLED`) incrementally re-indexes pages shared with a Notion internal integration into a separate `notion_wiki` collection (`type=notion`). A Notion share is inherited and multi-writer, so this text is unreviewed relative to curated company docs; the retriever labels it as such and ranks it below COMPANY. Un-shared pages are purged on the next tick.
- **FAILURES** — recorded failure cases (queried by `retrieve_failures`) teaching specialists what to avoid.
- **RECENT_RESEARCH** — web-research artifacts persisted from `executive_research` runs, kept separate from COMPANY so unvetted machine-generated text never blends into curated knowledge, and ranked below company documents.

Each parallel specialist call runs its own domain-filtered query. When no explicit filter is passed, `DOMAIN_ALIASES` maps the specialist key to its domains — e.g. `cso`→`strategy`, `cpo`→`product`,`strategy`, `board_comms`→`board`,`finance`. Hits beyond a cosine distance threshold are dropped, and very short messages (greetings) bypass retrieval entirely.

Multi-domain chunks fan out to one row per declared domain, so `_dedupe_by_text` drops duplicate-text hits while preserving relevance order before results are returned.

The formatted context is injected into the **user turn** (wrapped in `<relevant_knowledge>` by `BaseAgent.analyze`), never into a cached system block — per-query hits would otherwise poison the prompt cache.

### Store start-up resilience

`ChromaDBStore` only treats specific corruption signatures as recoverable — the Rust bindings' "range start index … out of range for slice" panic, SQLite's "file is not a database" / "database disk image is malformed", or hnswlib's "index … corrupted". It then **renames** the directory aside to `<dir>.corrupt-<timestamp>` with `os.rename`, which moves it whole or not at all (never `shutil.move`, whose copy-then-delete fallback would delete live files on Windows), and opens a fresh store. Every other failure — a locked file, a second client with different settings, permissions — propagates untouched; any other pyo3 `PanicException` (a `BaseException`) leaves the store in place and is re-raised as `RuntimeError` so degraded-mode handlers catch it. Because chromadb caches a System per path *before* starting it, a failed open stops and uncaches the System it created (never one a working client registered earlier), so the store can be reopened in-process once the problem clears. The API lifespan then starts without a warm store: `app.state.store` is left unset so the routes' `_get_store` helpers and per-call retrieval build their own store once the problem clears. Until it does, retrieval — and the chat turns that use it — still fail: this keeps the rest of the API up, it does not make chat RAG-free. Opening is serialized per process (retrieval opens stores from worker threads), and a seeding failure — including a panic from a corrupt index on its first add or query — is logged without discarding an open store.
